# RawInputs

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Mouse](BlitzBasic-Mouse)

</div>


```blitzbasic
RawInputs enable:Int32
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enable` | Int32 | required | 1 (True) to ask for the raw mouse, 0 (False) for the same as the original. |

## Description

Asks for the mouse as the hardware reports it, without the pointer acceleration and rounding of the system. It is off by default, which gives exactly what the original does.

With it on, [MouseXSpeed](MouseXSpeed) and [MouseYSpeed](MouseYSpeed) count the movement of the mouse itself, whatever the pointer settings of the system are, and keep the part of a pixel that is left over until the next call, so slow movements are not lost. It needs no [MoveMouse](MoveMouse) to do this: the window keeps the pointer while the program asks for the speed and lets go about 300 milliseconds after the last time it did. [MouseX](MouseX) and [MouseY](MouseY) go on telling where the pointer would be. The wheel is counted by its fractions too: a wheel or touchpad that scrolls in small steps adds them up and [MouseZ](MouseZ) and [MouseZSpeed](MouseZSpeed) change by one whenever a whole step is there. Joysticks and keyboards are not changed, as the system gives their values as they are anyway.

On a platform without a mouse that can be asked for like this (see [HWRawInputs](HWRawInputs)) the setting is accepted and everything reports as it does with it off.

## Differences

* This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the original has no such command, and gets its mouse speed from DirectInput.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
RawInputs True
Local x# = 160
While Not KeyHit(1)
	x = x + MouseXSpeed() ; Not accelerated, no MoveMouse needed.
	Cls
	Text 10, 10, "Move the mouse sideways, Escape ends"
	Oval x - 8, 110, 16, 16, 1
	Flip
Wend
```
